units.function: Mocked route tests distinguishing withdrawal of a queued comment from privacy-preserving tombstone deletion of an already-normal comment, including derived annotation/reference/training cleanup.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest -> Issue routes -> mocked Issue/Run/access/activity plus annotation, reference, external-object and decision-training services; one tx token is propagated through tombstone cleanup callbacks.
units.keyDataModels: Issue/current Run, human-authored comment timestamps, tombstone deletion attribution, cancellation receipt and derived annotation/reference/training records.
units.lifecycle: Author requests cancel or delete -> classify queued by active Run/time -> physically remove unconsumed queued comment or tombstone normal comment -> scrub derived copies/references -> record content-free activity receipt.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed run failed 6/6 on TCP bind; approved unsandboxed run passed 6/6. Behavior and privacy intent are clear, but all services/transactions are mocked and race, rollback, Agent authors, legal hold and durable consumption state are absent.
units.designRationale: Let a human retract input before an Agent consumes it, while deleting later comments without erasing the fact, actor and consequences of deletion or leaving sensitive copies in derived systems.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must reconcile user deletion rights with immutable organizational responsibility and evidence, and must know whether an instruction was delivered/consumed before allowing irreversible withdrawal.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT separate WithdrawQueuedInstruction and TombstoneComment commands, author-only default, content-free deletion receipts, derived-copy scrub registry and single transaction boundary. Replace timestamp inference with durable delivery/claim state and CAS, add idempotency, legal-hold/retention policy, evidence digest or exempted proof, compliance authority, Agent/on-behalf attribution and verified cross-store erasure jobs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Physical removal based on a time heuristic may erase an instruction an Agent already consumed, while ordinary deletion may remove evidence without legal-hold evaluation. Cleanup success is not proven atomic despite a shared tx token.
evidence: git history: 13 commits from ded813ad6fae2c0b2c9009e04f59b117ecae0151 through 73eb23734f25c570d88665e672f80d740797c632 recorded in read ledger
2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 0/6 passed due TCP listen EPERM
units.securityFindings: HIGH cancellation-race gap: queued/consumed state is inferred from Run presence/timestamps without CAS. HIGH erasure-governance gap: legal hold, retention basis and evidence exemption are absent. HIGH atomicity gap: mocks do not prove all derived cleanup rolls back together; safe sync may swallow errors. MEDIUM identity gap: Agent/on-behalf and compliance actors are untested. MEDIUM replay gap: repeated cancel/delete is absent. MEDIUM error-contract gap: English strings are asserted instead of stable codes.
